title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Models on Google Cloud to Reach All 3 Major US Clouds

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Google's Model Garden now provides access to GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna under a new distribution agreement with OpenAI. This expansion extends OpenAI's availability to the Gemini Agent and Antigravity coding tools, meaning the company now has a presence on all three major US cloud platforms. Google is now the only hyperscale provider to host the three leading closed-source large language models—those from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google—alongside more than 200 other models.

Enterprise clients can purchase the models through the Google Cloud Marketplace using existing cloud spending commitments, while users of Google AI Pro or Ultra can utilize monthly credits. The partnership follows the end of OpenAI's exclusive distribution deal with Microsoft on April 27, 2026, and a subsequent launch on Amazon Web Services in April. Google has provided computing capacity to OpenAI under a deal signed in 2025.

selectedTweets.text:
OpenAI and Google reach a major AI distribution agreement

OpenAI will offer GPT-6 Astra and Codex in Google Cloud’s Model Garden within weeks, which puts its models on all 3 major US clouds.

Customers can buy the models through Google Cloud Marketplace and count the purchases against cloud spending they have already committed, which removes a separate procurement step.

Regulated customers can run OpenAI models inside Google Cloud’s access controls and data governance tools when building agentic workflows.

The deal became possible only after April 27, 2026, when Microsoft’s license to OpenAI’s technology turned non-exclusive and Microsoft stopped paying OpenAI a revenue share on Azure resales.

Amazon Web Services was first through that opening, with Codex available on Bedrock by June, while Microsoft remains OpenAI’s primary cloud partner and gets new products first.

Google, a direct OpenAI competitor, had asked the FTC in December 2024 to break up the Microsoft exclusivity, and it also supplies OpenAI with computing capacity under a 2025 deal.
